correctness.rationale: Complete finite proof using two standalone independent representations of the twelve-vertex cubic graph. Standard forcing is equivalent to hitting all inclusion-minimal forts: verify_forts.py examines all 4095 nonempty sets, isolates 66 minimal forts from 851 forts, excludes all seeds of size at most three and finds exactly 89 forcing four-sets. verify_direct.py independently checks 794 initial candidates by parallel closure and computes all 3916 pairs of minimum sets, 366 exchanges, exact speed histogram (8,32,43,6), filtered component orders/edge counts, efficient triangular-prism-plus-edge graph and all connected diameters. Both agree on a SHA-256 digest of the complete 89-set roster under the explicit graph isomorphism. The original paths were executed successfully; no infinite extrapolation is asserted. Critical scope: unrestricted one-vertex token jump, standard synchronous forcing, this fixed Frucht graph only.

value.rationale: The Frucht graph is a canonical asymmetric cubic graph, not an arbitrary parameterized instance. The combined question—whether all optimal-initial-size and optimal-speed control placements can be reconfigured without losing either optimum—is natural after the separate propagation-time and zero-forcing exchange theories. The answer is a motivated structural obstruction: the eight efficient configurations form a triangular prism disjoint from an edge, while allowing one extra propagation round produces a connected 40-state graph. The exact diameter increase from six unrestricted to eight with a time-four cap quantifies mobility cost. This is a complete finite threshold and counterexample, beyond a count or routine parameter substitution; it does not claim a family-wide theorem.
